definitions.relation: A set of ordered pairs associating inputs with outputs.
definitions.function: A relation assigning exactly one output to each input in its domain.
definitions.input: A value supplied to a rule or function.
definitions.output: The value a function or rule returns for a specified input.
definitions.function notation: Notation such as f(x) representing the output of function f at input x.
definitions.domain: The set of inputs for which a relation or function is defined.
definitions.range: The set of outputs actually produced by the allowed inputs.
definitions.discrete: Data or a function defined at separate distinct input values.
definitions.continuous: A quantity or graph defined across an interval with no gaps or jumps at points of the interval.
definitions.representation: One of several ways to express a relationship, such as a table, graph, words, or equation.
definitions.parent function: A basic function used as the reference for transformed versions.
definitions.transformation: A change to a function graph such as a shift, reflection, or stretch.
definitions.translation: A rigid horizontal or vertical shift of a graph.
definitions.reflection: Flipping a graph across an axis or another specified line.
definitions.stretch: Multiplying a graph's distances from an axis by a constant scale factor.
definitions.piecewise function: A function described by different rules for different portions of its domain.
definitions.sequence: An ordered list of values indexed by positive integers or another specified index set.
definitions.common difference: The fixed difference between consecutive terms of an arithmetic sequence.
definitions.inverse relation: The relation obtained by reversing the input and output coordinates.
definitions.one-to-one: A relation in which each output comes from at most one input; it passes the horizontal-line test when a function.
